analysis:
Both units are base-side excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 34946-36361). The file is a public golden-vector fixture (synthetic 'cache-parity' inputs, gpt-oss-20b token IDs, prompt_contract_id and chain_hash block boundaries). The patch excerpt shows head-side changes: added additional_context {enable_thinking:false} in a request body, changed prompt_token_count from 803 to 767, regenerated chain hashes, dropped a 768-token block boundary, and altered token_ids. Changes are data-only test fixtures with no code, auth, attestation, crypto key or routing logic.

The visible base content holds no secrets or real consumer data, only public synthetic strings. Relevant threat context is the prefix-cache threat T-041 (chain_hash / block-boundary derivation) and the prompt-contract parity between coordinator and provider. The fixtures do not themselves change any security control. The remaining uncertainty is outside the supplied evidence: the head-side token_ids and the prompt-contract implementation that consumes these vectors (the provider/template code changes that presumably introduce additional_context). I could not verify that the cache-key or prompt_contract_id derivation correctly incorporates additional_context.enable_thinking, which matters for cross-tenant cache-sharing isolation under T-041. The head patch is truncated and only base text was supplied, so I make no finding. A follow-up pass should check that additional_context participates in prompt_contract_id / chain-hash derivation and that the fixture changes match the code change.
